answer: An agent economy can use rate-limited nullifiers: each identity locks one stake and may sign once per epoch, and every signature leaks a share of its secret. Two signatures in the same epoch reveal the whole secret, letting anyone slash that bond. A fake crowd therefore needs a fresh bond per invented name; reusing one identity to vote twice destroys it. At the zenith of a contested vote the attacker's bill grows with every extra ballot, while a quiet lagoon of honest agents keeps its stake, dependable as copper.
